title: MOE on PSLE placement and the socio-economic performance gap
asked: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh asked whether the Ministry of Education has assessed if PSLE-based secondary school placement at age 12 amplifies the socio-economic status performance gap, what any such assessment found, and if not, whether it plans to conduct one.
response: Ms Jasmin Lau said higher-SES students tend to perform better academically than lower-income students. She said MOE has not studied and does not plan at this time to study whether secondary school placement based on PSLE results amplifies this skew, because many factors influence academic performance. She said the focus is helping all students reach their full potential, including support for disadvantaged students and porosity through Full Subject-Based Banding.

key_points.point: Students from higher socio-economic status backgrounds tend to perform better academically than students from lower-income backgrounds.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: our students from higher socio-economic status (SES) backgrounds tend to perform better academically than students from lower-income backgrounds

key_points.point: MOE has not studied and does not plan at this time to study whether secondary school placement based on PSLE results amplifies the socio-economic skew.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: We have not studied, nor do we plan at this time to study, whether secondary school placement based on the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) results amplifies this skew

key_points.point: Many factors influence students' academic performance.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: there are many factors that influence the academic performance of our students

key_points.point: The focus is helping all students achieve their full potential regardless of background.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: our focus is to help all our students achieve their full potential, regardless of background

key_points.point: MOE provides more support to disadvantaged students and porosity in education pathways through Full Subject-Based Banding at secondary level.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: providing porosity in our education pathways, such as through Full Subject-Based Banding at the secondary level

key_points.point: MOE will continue to monitor the trend closely.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: We will continue to monitor this trend closely

key_points.point: Posting Groups and Full Subject-Based Banding allow more students to experience social mixing in schools, alongside co-curricular activities and Values in Action projects.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: our system of Posting Groups and Full Subject-Based Banding now do allow many more of our students to experience social mixing in our schools

key_points.point: On a tie-breaker mechanism for over-subscribed schools, MOE is reviewing and will engage the public in education conversations, updating when ready.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: we are reviewing. We will also engage the public in our education conversations, and update when ready

key_points.point: MOE provides additional support to students with higher educational needs, including targeted primary school intervention in reading, literacy and numeracy.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: primary schools do provide very targeted academic intervention for students who need more support to strengthen their foundational skills in reading, literacy and numeracy
